description: A lead technology counsel must approve the public release of an internal machine-learning toolkit and set the licensing, scope, export, and data-cleansing conditions, with input from open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy counsel.

shared_context.S1: The engineering team plans to publish the Atlas machine-learning toolkit in the company's public repository next Friday.
shared_context.S2: The toolkit is intended for external developers and includes source code, documentation, and a sample training package.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez gives the final legal approval for the public release and records any conditions in the release ticket.
shared_context.S4: The firm's weekly product-release legal gate includes a checklist update from open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy counsel before the final approval is recorded.

PF1.text: While reviewing the build manifest this week, Noah confirmed that the public distribution links the toolkit with a GPLv3 library, so the combined distribution must use the GPLv3 license and include corresponding source and attribution notices; he has not updated the release ticket.

PF2.text: Maya reviewed the largest customer's source-code agreement and confirmed that the customer's proprietary connector is included in the current build; the agreement prohibits public release of that connector without written customer consent, so the public package must exclude the connector and be limited to the core toolkit; she has not added this contract restriction to the release checklist.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with the export-classification team this week that Atlas contains covered encryption functionality and requires a SNAP-R self-classification filing before public release; the classification confirmation is in his working file but not in the release ticket.

PF4.text: Sofia's review of the sample training package found exactly 312 pseudonymized customer records; privacy approval requires removing all 312 records and documenting the removal before any public release, and she has not yet entered that gate in the product checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The release must be approved subject to all listed legal conditions.
The combined distribution must use the GPLv3 license.
The public package must be limited to the core toolkit.
The customer proprietary connector must be excluded.
A SNAP-R self-classification filing must be completed before release.
Exactly 312 training records must be removed before release.
The release must include source and attribution notices.
The customer connector exclusion must be documented in the release ticket.
The export filing must be documented before release.
The privacy removal gate must be documented before release.

decisive_facts.why: The build manifest changes the required license from an unspecified public-release license to exactly GPLv3 and adds the required source and attribution notice commitment.
The customer agreement changes the public package from the full build to exactly the core toolkit, requires exclusion of the connector, and adds documentation of that exclusion.
The export classification changes the pre-release condition from no specified filing to completion and documentation of a SNAP-R self-classification filing.
The privacy review changes the training-package condition to removal of exactly 312 records and documentation of a privacy removal gate before release.
